items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: No mention of Frank Sinatra by Dave Brubeck; Sinatra is only mentioned by the interviewer in a different context.

ctx.x: Who suggested that? Did that come from George Avakian?

That came from me. My friend in the Army taught me all the Matt Dennis tunes. He was Festus in “Gunsmoke.” Ken Curtis. He could sing with the big bands and often took the place of Frank Sinatra or somebody. He was that good.

Let me talk about once again your relationship with Columbia. After Take Five, you have a huge hit single, unusual. It’s unusual for any jazz musician to have a hit single, but for an instrumental and in 5/4, these are unique events. After that, was there pressure on you from Columbia to become more of a hit-maker and do more commercial music? Or did they give you freedom to define what you wanted?
